In this tutorial, we explore some of the infrastructure and platform requirements for large model training, and to support the training of many models by many teams. We focus specifically on experiment tracking (using [MLFlow](https://mlflow.org/)).

Follow along at [ML Experiment Tracking with MLFlow](https://teaching-on-testbeds.github.io/mlflow-chi/).

Note: this tutorial requires advance reservation of specific hardware! You will need a node with 2 GPUs suitable for model training. You should reserve a 3-hour block.

You can use either:

* a `gpu_mi100` at CHI@TACC, or
* a `compute_liqid` at CHI@TACC

# 2_create_server.ipynb

## [markdown]

## Launch and set up NVIDIA A100 40GB server - with python-chi

At the beginning of the lease time, we will bring up our GPU server. We will use the `python-chi` Python API to Chameleon to provision our server.

> **Note**: if you reserved an AMD GPU server, [follow the AMD instructions](index_amd), then open `2_create_server.ipynb`.

We will execute the cells in this notebook inside the Chameleon Jupyter environment.

Run the following cell, and make sure the correct project is selected:

## [code]

```python
# run in Chameleon Jupyter environment
from chi import server, context, lease
import os

context.version = "1.0" 
context.choose_project()
context.choose_site(default="CHI@TACC")
```

## [markdown]

Change the string in the following cell to reflect the name of *your* lease (**with your own net ID**), then run it to get your lease:

## [code]

```python
# run in Chameleon Jupyter environment
l = lease.get_lease(f"mlflow_netID") 
l.show()
```

## [markdown]

The status should show as “ACTIVE” now that we are past the lease start time.

# docker/docker-compose-mlflow-garage.yaml

```yaml
name: tracking_service
services:
  # Garage object store service provides storage for artifacts, models
  garage:
    image: dxflrs/garage:v2.2.0
    container_name: garage
    restart: always
    expose:
      - "3900"
    ports:
      - "3900:3900"  # S3 API (use Garage default)
    command: ["/garage", "-c", "/etc/garage.toml", "server"]
    volumes:
      - garage_data:/var/lib/garage/data
      - garage_meta:/var/lib/garage/meta
      - ./garage-bootstrap/garage.toml:/etc/garage.toml:ro
  
  # Sets up a Garage bucket and credentials for MLFlow
  garage-init:
    image: docker:26-cli
    depends_on:
      - garage
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - ./garage-bootstrap:/bootstrap
      - ./garage-bootstrap/garage.toml:/etc/garage.toml:ro
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/bootstrap/garage-init.sh"]

  # Postgresql server provides storage for parameters, metrics from experiment runs
  postgres:
    image: postgres:18
    container_name: postgres
    restart: always
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: user
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: password
      POSTGRES_DB: mlflowdb
    ports:
      - "5433:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql  # use a volume so storage persists beyond container lifetime

  mlflow:
    image: ghcr.io/mlflow/mlflow:v3.9.0
    container_name: mlflow
    restart: always
    depends_on:
      garage:
        condition: service_started
      postgres:
        condition: service_started
      garage-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI: http://0.0.0.0:8000
      MLFLOW_LOGGING_LEVEL: ERROR
      MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL: http://garage:3900  # how mlflow will access object store
      MLFLOW_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS: "*"
    volumes:
      - ./garage-bootstrap:/bootstrap:ro
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    command: >
      /bin/sh -c "set -a &&
      . /bootstrap/creds.env &&
      set +a &&
      pip install psycopg2-binary boto3 &&
      mlflow server --backend-store-uri postgresql://user:password@postgres/mlflowdb
      --artifacts-destination s3://mlflow-artifacts/ --serve-artifacts --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000"

volumes:
  postgres_data:
  garage_data:
  garage_meta:
```

# docker/docker-compose-mlflow.yaml

```yaml
name: tracking_service
services:
  # MinIO object store service provides storage for artifacts, models
  minio:
    image: minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z
    container_name: minio
    restart: always
    expose:
      - "9000"
    ports:  
      - "9000:9000"  # The API for object storage is hosted on port 9000
      - "9001:9001"  # The web-based UI is on port 9001
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: "your-access-key"
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: "your-secret-key"
    healthcheck:
      test: timeout 5s bash -c ':> /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000' || exit 1
      interval: 1s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    volumes:
      - minio_data:/data  # Use a volume so minio storage persists beyond container lifetime

  # When the minio service has started, launch a container with the minio client
  # and use it to create a bucket named mlflow-artifacts
  minio-create-bucket:
    image: minio/mc:RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z-cpuv1
    depends_on:
      minio:
        condition: service_healthy
    entrypoint: >
      /bin/sh -c "
      mc alias set minio http://minio:9000 your-access-key your-secret-key &&
      if ! mc ls minio/mlflow-artifacts; then
        mc mb minio/mlflow-artifacts &&
        echo 'Bucket mlflow-artifacts creatd'
      else
        echo 'Bucket mlflow-artifacts already exists';
      fi"

  # Postgresql server provides storage for parameters, metrics from experiment runs
  postgres:
    image: postgres:18
    container_name: postgres
    restart: always
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: user
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: password
      POSTGRES_DB: mlflowdb
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql  # use a volume so storage persists beyond container lifetime

  mlflow:
    image: ghcr.io/mlflow/mlflow:v3.9.0
    container_name: mlflow
    restart: always
    depends_on:
      - minio
      - postgres
      - minio-create-bucket  # make sure minio and posgres services are alive, and bucket is created, before mlflow starts
    environment:
      MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI: http://0.0.0.0:8000
      MLFLOW_LOGGING_LEVEL: ERROR
      MLFLOW_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS: "*"
      MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL: http://minio:9000  # how mlflow will access object store
      AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: "your-access-key"
      AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: "your-secret-key"
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    command: >
      /bin/sh -c "pip install psycopg2-binary boto3 &&
      mlflow server --backend-store-uri postgresql://user:password@postgres/mlflowdb 
      --artifacts-destination s3://mlflow-artifacts/ --serve-artifacts --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000"

volumes:
  minio_data:
  postgres_data:
```
